fields.problem:
Title: Fundamental Theorem of Galois Theory

Let $L / K$ be a [[Definition:Finite Field Extension|finite]] [[Definition:Galois Extension|Galois extension]].

Let $\Gal {L / K}$ denote the [[Definition:Galois Group of Field Extension|Galois group]] of the [[Definition:Field Extension |extension]] $L / K$.

Let $H$ denote a [[Definition:Subgroup|subgroup]] of $\Gal {L / K}$ and $F$ denote an [[Definition:Intermediate Field|intermediate field]].

Let $L_H$ denote the [[Definition:Fixed Field|fixed field]] of $H$.

The [[Definition:Mapping|mappings]]:

:$H \mapsto L_H$, and

:$F \mapsto \Gal {L / F}$

are [[Definition:Inclusion-Reversing|inclusion-reversing]] and [[Definition:Inverse Mapping|inverses]].

Moreover, these maps induce a [[Definition:Bijection|bijection]] between the [[Definition:Normal Subgroup|normal subgroups]] of $\Gal {L / K}$ and the [[Definition:Normal Extension|normal]], [[Definition:Intermediate Field|intermediate]] extensions of $L / K$.

fields.witness: Let K=𝔽₂ and F=𝔽₂[α]/(α²+α+1), so α²=α+1. Define τ:F→F by τ(z)=z² (Frobenius). Then τ fixes K because 0²=0 and 1²=1. It is an automorphism, with τ²(z)=z⁴=z for all z∈F; hence τ∈Gal(F/K). But τ(α)=α²=α+1≠α, since 1≠0. Thus τ does not fix F pointwise.
